3	GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.
4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
8	- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
9	- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
10	- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
11	- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
12	- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
13	- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.
14	
15	Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.
16	
17	Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.
18	
19	## Rules
20	
21	- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
22	- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
23	- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
24	- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
25	- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
26	- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
27	- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
28	- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
29	- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
30	- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
31	- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.
32

41	pnpm lint
42	pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
43	pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs

# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

1	# GraphGoblin Documentation
2	
3	Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.
4	
5	GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.
6	
7	GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.
8	
9	## Reading order
10	
11	| #   | Document                                                     | What it covers                                                                                                  |
12	| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
13	| -   | [User guide](guide/README.md)                                | Install locally, build loops, run and observe, configure triggers and integrations                              |
14	| 01  | [Vision and scope](01-vision-and-scope.md)                   | Purpose, target users, mental model, principles, 1.0 scope, post-1.0 roadmap                                    |
15	| 02  | [Architecture](02-architecture.md)                           | Stack, layering, package layout, ports, process topology, cross-cutting concerns                                |
16	| -   | [Architecture snapshot](architecture/README.md)              | Structural map of the code at `c379f80`: packages, data, storage, API, web, adapters, triggers, one traced loop |
17	| -   | [Debt register](architecture/debt-register.md)               | Technical debt items, reconciled issues, prioritized follow-ups and owner decisions (#163)                      |
18	| 03  | [Domain model](03-domain-model.md)                           | Loops, versions, nodes, runs, events, invocations, the context thread                                           |
19	| 04  | [Node catalog](04-node-catalog.md)                           | Every node type: purpose, configuration, ports, engine behaviour                                                |
20	| 05  | [Execution engine](05-execution-engine.md)                   | Executor semantics, event sourcing, run lifecycle, resiliency model                                             |
21	| 06  | [Harness integration](06-harness-integration.md)             | Harness port, Codex/Claude/Ollama inference, model discovery and Chat workflow integration                      |
22	| 07  | [API, streaming, and MCP](07-api-and-streaming.md)           | REST surface, SSE, OpenAPI, auth, MCP server, Codex and Claude Code plugins                                     |
23	| 08  | [Triggers and integrations](08-triggers-and-integrations.md) | Manual, cron, webhook, inbound event, polling; security of inbound paths                                        |
24	| 09  | [Frontend and PWA](09-frontend-and-pwa.md)                   | Native Chat, paired Goblin PWA, editor, run inspector, settings and service-worker update flow                  |
25	| 10  | [Testing and quality](10-testing-and-quality.md)             | Coverage policy, fixtures, adversarial QA agents, CI gates                                                      |

# GraphGoblin Documentation

Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.

GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.

## Reading order

| -   | [Architecture snapshot](architecture/README.md)              | Structural map of the code at `c379f80`: packages, data, storage, API, web, adapters, triggers, one traced loop |
| -   | [Debt register](architecture/debt-register.md)               | Technical debt items, reconciled issues, prioritized follow-ups and owner decisions (#163)                      |
| 03  | [Domain model](03-domain-model.md)                           | Loops, versions, nodes, runs, events, invocations, the context thread                                           |
| 04  | [Node catalog](04-node-catalog.md)                           | Every node type: purpose, configuration, ports, engine behaviour                                                |
| 05  | [Execution engine](05-execution-engine.md)                   | Executor semantics, event sourcing, run lifecycle, resiliency model                                             |
| 06  | [Harness integration](06-harness-integration.md)             | Harness port, Codex/Claude/Ollama inference, model discovery and Chat workflow integration                      |
| 07  | [API, streaming, and MCP](07-api-and-streaming.md)           | REST surface, SSE, OpenAPI, auth, MCP server, Codex and Claude Code plugins                                     |
| 08  | [Triggers and integrations](08-triggers-and-integrations.md) | Manual, cron, webhook, inbound event, polling; security of inbound paths                                        |
| 09  | [Frontend and PWA](09-frontend-and-pwa.md)                   | Native Chat, paired Goblin PWA, editor, run inspector, settings and service-worker update flow                  |
| 10  | [Testing and quality](10-testing-and-quality.md)             | Coverage policy, fixtures, adversarial QA agents, CI gates                                                      |
| 11  | [Security and distribution](11-security-and-distribution.md) | Licensing, credentials, secrets, inbound exposure, retention                                                    |
| 12  | [Implementation plan](12-implementation-plan.md)             | Milestones M0 to M8 with tasks and acceptance criteria                                                          |
| 13  | [Open questions](13-open-questions.md)                       | Items that still need a decision, and which milestone they block                                                |

| -   | [reference/nodes.md](reference/nodes.md)                     | Node config reference, generated from the schemas (`pnpm docs:generate`)                                        |
| -   | [reference/api.md](reference/api.md)                         | REST API reference, generated from the OpenAPI document                                                         |
| -   | [decisions/](decisions/)                                     | Architecture decision records                                                                                   |
| -   | [research/](research/)                                       | Preserved research on Codex, Claude Code, Jev, licences, and runtimes                                           |

## Status legend

- **Decided**: agreed with the product owner. Change it through a new ADR.

1	# 15 - Issue workflow
2	
3	GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.
4	
5	## Gates
6	
7	- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
8	- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
9	- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
10	- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.
11	
12	`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.
13	
14	## Post-merge human QA
15	
16	Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.
17	
18	A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.
19	
20	## Parking markers
21	
22	Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.
23	
24	- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
25	- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.
26	
27	## QA scope
28	
29	- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.
30	- `qa:full-regression`: also retest the whole application end to end, covering positive and negative scenarios, and catalogue the results.
31	
32	Name the QA agent in the issue body's Delivery section, not with a label.
33	
34	Retain QA evidence under `docs/qa/` with repository-relative citations and preserve raw JSON, YAML and JavaScript/TypeScript bytes so recorded hashes remain valid; `.prettierignore` excludes those artifacts while QA Markdown remains formatted.
35	
36	## Model routing
37	
38	The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:
39	
40	| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
41	| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
42	| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
43	| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
44	| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
45	| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |
46	
47	Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.
48	
49	## Types, areas, and milestones
50	
51	Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.
52	
53	Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.
54	
55	Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.
56	
57	## Development pipeline
58	
59	An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.
60	
61	The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

# #362 bounded regression and guidance

Candidate: `5db3dfd4e2c96e53aa52b5a33403819da8c49196`, tree `c6fc1acd4e0837ed4ec3cad0e8554f926e0f8626`, parent `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`. Root GPT implemented the four-file documentation/test change under D179. This is author evidence, separate from the actual Claude independent native/public QA on unchanged production at the parent.

Current production already contains the synchronous start-refusal fix. No runtime source, public contract, shell default, dependency or migration changes here. The existing native Windows regression now covers both .cmd and .bat. Each direct invocation must refuse without creating its marker; the exact same authored batch file must then execute through an explicit absolute cmd.exe /d /c invocation and produce the expected marker. The positive control prevents a broken fixture from masquerading as a safe refusal.

Numbered node documentation, troubleshooting and CHANGELOG explain the current SCRIPT_START_FAILED contract, ordinary Resume after proven non-start, explicit shell interpretation/quoting and the need for a corrected definition/new run when changing the pinned command. Internal PROCESS_START_FAILED stderr and the historical report are not renamed into a new public error.

Checks used project Node v22.23.4 and pnpm 12.8.1 after an offline frozen install. The install reused 801 packages with no downloads or lockfile change. `checks.ps1` retained the exact scoped commands. Native-focused Vitest: **4 passed / 43 out-of-scope skipped**, exit0 (both native extensions, synchronous refusal control and missing command). Infrastructure typecheck, touched-test ESLint, four-file Prettier and git diff check passed; the whole check script exited0. These are not a full infrastructure test/coverage or monorepo gate. No provider, owner store or live application was started by these author checks.

Independent actual Claude evidence remains in `i4-362-independent-01/publication`, including the initial failing setup/fixture attempts. Its authoritative accounting is 63 PASS plus one adjacent OBSERVED-AS-PREDICTED, not the original report's 64-PASS wording. Production equality to that tested base is established by this candidate's complete changed path list: the only package file changed is scripts.test.ts; all other changes are documentation. The independent build was not rebuilt or re-executed for this documentation/test child.

Opposite-family review, independent QA/source binding, exact-head/current-target CI and a fresh Astra MAX final audit remain open. No issue closure or owner acceptance is claimed.

110	conversation within this run and harness, including after restart; forks and children
111	start fresh. Its optional `resetAfterVisits` accepts positive safe integers, without a
112	default. N completed visits share a conversation; visit N+1 starts fresh. Retries and
113	repairs stay in their visit. Reset never clears shared context or another node's session.
114	Previous/named selection remains unchanged. See [ADR-0052](decisions/ADR-0052-node-own-session-continuity.md).
115	
116	Before invoking the harness, the engine durably records `harness.turn`: the exact rendered
117	prompt, selected resume ID, prompt kind and logical visit/turn identities. `harness.submission`
118	records refusal, uncertainty, missing-session status and any positive acceptance marker.
119	A definitely-not-submitted turn retries that saved task with its original session-policy
120	selection when the cause is resumable. Uncertain authored work cannot continue a previous/named/own
121	conversation on its inherited ID alone: this visit needs durable acceptance or a newly
122	established session. Repairs and continuations can use the visit's own session. Without a
123	usable session, the run fails non-resumably. Missing sessions have the explicit recovery choice below; Replay from the node
124	is the available deliberate new attempt. Named-session lookup still applies on replay.
125	See [submission recovery](05-execution-engine.md#inference-submission-and-recovery).
126	
127	Claude Code accepts only the explicit `read-only`/`never` or `danger-full-access`/`never` policy
128	pairs. `workspace-write`, `on-request`, explicit `networkAccess: false`, `webSearch: true`,
129	nonempty `capabilities`, and nonempty raw overrides are rejected during validation and again at
130	runtime. Its read-only policy limits built-in tools; it does not confine filesystem reads or the
131	operating system. See [Claude Code](06-harness-integration.md#claude-code-adapter-26).

150	For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Recovery classifies it as `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` with a visit ID and no dispatch ID; it does not run the command. The same failure and recovery choices remain available if writing a dispatched script's progress or completion failed. Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.

Repair the storage fault, inspect any external effect, then choose Resume or Replay knowingly, or leave the run failed with Cancel. No store reset or migration is required.

### Windows batch commands

Script commands run without an implicit shell. On Windows, naming a `.cmd` or `.bat` file as
the command fails with `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`: the process runner proved that it did not start.
This is distinct from `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, which needs explicit recovery consent because
an earlier attempt may have produced effects. A proven start refusal permits ordinary Resume,
but Resume still uses the failed run's pinned command and arguments.

To run a batch file, explicitly choose `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` (use your Windows
installation's actual path), set its arguments to `/d`, `/c` and the intended batch command,
and choose the working directory deliberately. `/d` disables the command processor's AutoRun
commands. The command string after `/c` is interpreted by that shell; keep it authored and
quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
Publish the corrected definition and start a new run. Repeatedly resuming the old batch-file
command cannot apply that definition change. If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

269	A subloop creates a separate child run with its own version, thread, and log. The parent waits with kind `child` and continues only after the child finishes; the child's exit ends the child, not the parent, which goes on to its own next node and exit. Use **parent run** and **child runs** links to move between them. By default the parent gets `lastOutput.value` containing `status`, `outcome`, `result`, and `childRunId`; a downstream decision can branch on that status. A child whose exit returns `none` gives no `result` (the field is absent, not `null`). A child that ends through a Failure or Exhausted exit is ordinary data for the parent, which continues. A child that fails while running (a script error, a provider failure, a bug) fails the parent at its subloop node with the same failure code and resumability, as if that work had run inline; the parent's failure links the **failed child run**. Fix the cause and **Resume** the parent: it resumes the same child, whose failed node runs again. Cancelling a child cancels the parent waiting for it, and cancelling the parent cancels active children.

555	## Replay and debugging (Decided by implementation, 2026-10-03)
556	
557	Recovery eligibility is computed once by the server and exposed as `recovery` on `GET /runs/{id}` and MCP `get_run` (ADR-0061). Both commands require the reviewed `observedSeq` and recheck this policy. Resume continues the same ID and attempt follower; Replay creates a separate run with its own ID, invocation, log and effects.
558	
559	- Resume keeps main's status and recorded resumability rules. Paused waits keep their identity and deadlines. A completed `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE` failure remains resumable after fixing the program. Non-resumable stop, deadline and unconfirmed-termination failures remain unavailable for Resume. A failed parent owns recovery of its exact failed child. Accepted parent recovery durably binds the child ID, failure sequence, observation and consent on `run.resumed.childRecovery`; parent ownership persists while pending. A later child failure requires new review and consent. Missing provider sessions require #265's explicit fresh-start choice for Resume; Replay remains a deliberate new attempt. An uncertain script needs explicit `retryUncertainScript: true` before retry. The recovery snapshot uses indexed lifecycle/failure/Resume evidence (at most three decoded event payloads per examined run) and one reached-node seek per definition node; migration 0025 adds the partial reached-node index. It returns the same decision record read after that evidence; a raced newer record refuses as stale. Resume executes that validated status branch, so a paused node failing during validation cannot become an unconsented script retry.
560	- Replay can start at any node the source reached, in any source status, with usable pinned definition and recorded state. It does not pause or alter the source. An active source can advance between read and command, making the observation stale. The inspector and API/MCP choice explain that scripts, provider turns, child runs and deliveries from the selected node run again for the new run. `recovery.replay[].effects` names the knowable nodes on possible paths, including loopbacks; it does not predict which branch will execute. This explanation and deliberate Replay choice provide ordinary consent. A path into the current uncertain script additionally requires explicit script consent, even if the dispatch marker is missing or Resume is non-resumable.
561	- The fork seeds the source's initial thread replayed through the sequence before that node's first `node.started`. It keeps inherited messages, variables, outputs, counters, gate passes, iteration, pinned definition and subloop versions. Its `run.queued.initialThread` is the executable seed, including while queued. It has a fresh invocation with `replayOf: { runId, nodeId }`. It owns new sessions and child runs, and drops the source caller's return defaults. Nothing before the chosen node runs again unless the graph routes back to it.
562	- Fork admission atomically writes the row, initial state, first event and `(sourceRunId, nodeId, observedSeq)` intent. Migration 0024 adds nullable node and observed-sequence intent columns and a unique index using #412's canonical `replay_source_run_id`; it does not duplicate the source. A failed transaction consumes nothing. A lost commit acknowledgement finds the same admitted fork; a repeated caller receives `RECOVERY_STALE` with its exact `replayRunId`. Re-reading unchanged history does not mint another intent for that same node. New execution events give a new observation. No event is appended to the source, so terminal history, SSE completion and finalization records retain their original boundary.
563	
564	Neither action undoes or hides recorded effects. A fork leaves the source row, thread, result and events unchanged and never re-sends the source's own recorded deliveries. When the fork reaches its exit it performs its own deliveries normally. Exactly-once external effects are not claimed. See [ADR-0061](decisions/ADR-0061-recovery-eligibility.md) for the refusal table.

windows-launcher:
    name: Windows launcher
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      LIVE: '0'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        id: node
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
      - name: Install
        id: install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build
        id: build
        run: pnpm build
      # Native evidence (#496): a fresh, non-hidden folder directly below the runner temp,
      # outside the checkout and every fixture. The suite writes typed records only. Prepared
      # after the build, so its failure can never skip install, build or the native command; it
      # needs only the checkout and Node, so a failed install or build is still recorded.
      - name: Prepare native evidence
        id: evidence
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.node.outcome == 'success' }}
        env:
          GG_TEST_EVIDENCE_EVENT_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          GG_TEST_EVIDENCE_EVENT_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: node tooling/scripts/windows-launcher-evidence.mjs init
      - name: Native Windows launcher acceptance
        id: native
        # Runs after a successful build whatever evidence preparation did. A preparation failure
        # still fails the job, and the suite then receives no evidence folder.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.build.outcome == 'success' }}
        env:
          GG_TEST_WINDOWS_LAUNCHER_EVIDENCE_DIR: ${{ steps.evidence.outcome == 'success' && steps.evidence.outputs.dir || '' }}
        run: pnpm test:windows-launcher
      - name: Finalize native evidence
        id: finalize
        # Only a successfully prepared folder is finalized, and only finalized files are uploaded.
        if: ${{ always() && steps.evidence.outcome == 'success' }}
        env:
          GG_TEST_WINDOWS_LAUNCHER_EVIDENCE_DIR: ${{ steps.evidence.outputs.dir }}
          GG_TEST_WINDOWS_LAUNCHER_EVIDENCE_ID: ${{ steps.evidence.outputs.id }}
          GG_TEST_EVIDENCE_INSTALL_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.install.outcome }}
          GG_TEST_EVIDENCE_BUILD_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.build.outcome }}
          GG_TEST_EVIDENCE_NATIVE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.native.outcome }}
        run: node tooling/scripts/windows-launcher-evidence.mjs finalize
      - name: Upload native evidence
        if: ${{ always() && steps.finalize.outputs.paths != '' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: windows-launcher-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ steps.finalize.outputs.paths }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          include-hidden-files: false
  repository-checks:
    name: Repository checks

# Changelog

All notable changes to GraphGoblin. The design is in [docs/](docs/README.md); the user guide is [docs/guide/](docs/guide/README.md).

## Unreleased

- Document explicit Windows batch-file invocation and pinned-definition recovery for
  `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` (#362). Current process-start containment is retained; native regression
  tests now cover both `.cmd` and `.bat` refusals with a successful explicit-shell control.

- Clarify that an enabled Codex model and a ready preflight do not establish current access
  for the API user's login and provider endpoint. Recognized Codex inference-turn refusals retain
  the provider's explanation; LLM decisions retain only a safe failure category. The guide
  describes deliberate supported-model/login selection without automatic fallback or an
  API-key-only promise (#427).
- Reconcile Codex sandbox documentation and source comments: the authored sandbox permission
  level is explicit, while Windows backend selection remains inherited unless explicitly
  overridden. No sandbox permissions or backend behavior changed (#365).

- Windows launcher identity and ownership checks own their descendants in private Windows jobs
  (#459), drain both output streams within a bounded work window and collect failed checks
  before displaying errors. Initial checks retain the 15-second work cap, with up to two seconds
  for cleanup; held-store retries reserve that cleanup time and retain the last held guidance
  when a conclusive new sample cannot fit. Raw helper output is never displayed or logged.
  Ownership output is parsed once as strict JSON before whitespace normalization; duplicate
  decoded keys, unknown fields and JavaScript-only syntax refuse startup. Cleanup is confirmed
  only when the complete process/job/stream observation finishes before the two-second deadline;
  a later completion keeps the unconfirmed-cleanup outcome (D166).

## Contract reconciliation (current naming and behaviour)

- **Historical defect.** Before PR #375 (`35bd31ad^`), `ProcessScripts.run` called `spawn` inside the Promise
  executor with no catch. The handler had only `finally`, so the synchronous EINVAL rejected the promise and
  reached the executor's generic catch as `INTERNAL_ERROR` (source: `raw/04-source-evidence.txt`, last two
  excerpts).
- **Retired name.** `PROCESS_START_FAILED` was never a `RunErrorCode`: `git log -S` over engine/contracts
  source is empty. It was, and still is, only the runner's synthetic stderr text
  `spawn failed: PROCESS_START_FAILED` (`scripts.ts:132,197`). The current public code is `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`
  (`contracts/src/run.ts:58`), with state `definitely-not-started` (`run.ts:99`). I did not revive the
  retired name, and the engine never records it for script nodes (E, A).
- **Recovery semantics.** For a proven refusal, "explicit recovery consent" means the user's explicit
  Resume or Replay action (docs/05:489, "ordinary explicit Resume tries it again"; guide 03:273).
  `run-recovery.ts:85-126` grants `resume: allowed` with no `scriptConsent`. The extra `retryUncertainScript`
  consent and the `SCRIPT_CONSENT_REQUIRED` refusal apply only to `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`. Observed
  behaviour matches (E1/E2/A1/A2/A6). M2 shows the consent path only when the fix is removed.
- **Precedence (source).** In the handler, unconfirmed termination is checked first, then cancellation
  (`ctx.signal.aborted` → cancelled), then state (`script.ts:82-115`). In the executor catch, deadline is
  checked first, then abort/cancel, then the typed `RunFailureError` (`run-manager.ts:2626-2683`).
  `INTERNAL_ERROR` arises only for untyped throws.
- **`shell:false` (source and behaviour).** The option is hard-coded at `scripts.ts:126` (dist line 115).
  Behaviourally, the batch bodies that create markers under `cmd.exe` never ran through the runner, engine
  or API.

## Recovery eligibility and Replay (#256)

Read the inspector's explanation for the current action. Resume retains the run ID and follows its next attempt. A completed `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE` failure remains resumable: fix the program, then Resume. Non-resumable stop/deadline/unconfirmed-termination failures stay unavailable for Resume. A failed child directs recovery to its exact parent, which retries the same child.

Replay is a deliberate new run at a reached node, including inference and subloop nodes, across source run statuses. It runs scripts, provider turns, child runs and deliveries on the new path again; the picker names knowable nodes on possible paths. It never undoes source effects or re-sends source-owned delivery records; the fork performs its own deliveries. A missing session does not prohibit Replay, although a named policy may look up the same missing session again. Use Start fresh session for #265's explicit same-run recovery. A path into the current uncertain script also needs explicit consent that its effect may already have happened.

If `RECOVERY_STALE` names an existing replay ID, open that run. The admitted fork and its observed intent are one transaction; there is no separate consumed-intent-without-fork window. Otherwise refresh and review current eligibility. API/MCP commands send `observedSeq` from that read, and `retryUncertainScript: true` only after deliberate uncertain-script consent. See [ADR-0061](../decisions/ADR-0061-recovery-eligibility.md).

If a child says recovery belongs to its parent, open that exact parent even while a previously accepted Resume is pending. A new uncertain child failure needs fresh review and consent. A `RECOVERY_STALE` response means read the current recovery choices again before submitting a new intent; do not automatically retry an earlier consent.

content.text:
**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.** The runtime and the test change are fine. The fix for the documentation finding (O2) is incomplete: the user-guide line O2 specifically named still tells users to Resume, and the new text doesn't say that Replay also keeps the old command. The required changes are documentation only.

## What I reviewed
- **Original change:** source `5db3dfd4e2c96e53aa52b5a33403819da8c49196` (tree `c6fc1acd…`) against base `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`. I read the whole four-file diff from the author's retained `candidate.patch`.
- **Current integrated head:** the worktree's branch ref `codex/gg-i4-362-batch-guidance` reads `b3f22d345aee3cbfbcd818ebb7980d962cafd2b1`. Its merge parents, per the root records, are `d284b9a4…` and current main `a84f988b…`. In the working tree the four changed regions match the patch byte for byte as far as I can read.
- **Integration:** the three merge conflicts (`.gitattributes`, `.prettierignore`, `CHANGELOG.md`) are plain additions of both sides. The #362 and #427 path blocks don't overlap, and the CHANGELOG keeps #362, then #427/#365, then #459. No problems found.

## Blocking findings

**F1 (medium): the O2 guidance fix is incomplete and now contradicts itself.**
- QA's O2 cited guide 03:273 as the misleading text and showed that Replay also fails again (QA `REPORT.md:147-151`, case A1-replay at `:119`).
- `docs/guide/03-run-and-observe.md:273` is unchanged and still says "Fix the start configuration, then Resume." Guide 07:98 sends readers there "for every contract code."
- `docs/guide/07-troubleshooting.md:150` still says "correct the missing command or start configuration and explicitly Resume."
- The new instruction "publish a corrected definition and start a new run" (`docs/04-node-catalog.md:157`, `07:168`) sits next to text that calls Replay a new run (`04:152`, `07:150`, `07:519`). But Replay keeps the pinned definition (`05-execution-engine.md:561`); only a fresh run uses the latest published version (`03-domain-model.md:151`). A user who publishes a fix and then uses Replay gets the same failure again.
- **Required:** qualify 03:273 and 07:150 so Resume applies to external fixes (such as a missing executable). Say that a change to command, arguments or working directory needs a published fix and a fresh run, not Resume or Replay, and link to `#windows-batch-commands`. Mention Replay in 04:157 and 07:168. The failed retries cause no side effects, so this is a correctness problem in the guidance, not a safety one.

**F2 (low, introduced): heading nesting in guide 07.** The new `### Windows batch commands` (07:154) was inserted between the "Find the symptom" paragraphs and the general symptom table. That whole table (07:172–218) now sits under the batch heading in the page outline. Move the subsection after the table, before 07:219; the link from docs/04 stays valid if the heading text is unchanged. On its own this wouldn't block.

## Confirmed correct
- **Runtime:** the PR #375 catch is present (`scripts.ts:128-134`) and `shell: false` is hard-coded (`:126`). The engine maps the refusal to `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`, a resumable failure code (`engine/src/handlers/script.ts:105-114`). No runtime fix is needed, and none was invented.
- **Test (`scripts.test.ts:358-385`):** it catches the real regressions:
